steps.m:
Tidewell has closed the complaint. Its record shows complaint status closed with refunds confirmed and refund status paid. Nothing more is needed, so here is the recap.

**Outcome.** Complaint TC-30481 was upheld under decision DR-30481 on 15 May and closed on 23 May. Both refunds are posted on the Calder Mutual account and nothing is pending.

| Refund | From | Route | Posted |
|---|---|---|---|
| £48.50 service fee | Tidewell | Bank transfer to Calder account | 17 May |
| £394.00 stay charges | Quaymark (host) | Card refund to card ending 0938 | 18 May |

That is the full £442.50 paid for the stay, with no deduction.

**What went wrong.** The host, Quaymark, caused the lockout. On 21 April it changed its channel-manager rule so that overlapping bookings automatically keep the latest one and revoke the other guest's PIN. On 24 April at 17:58 its system imported a direct booking for the same flat, and at 18:02 it superseded your booking, revoked your PIN and suppressed any notification to you. Your four PIN attempts between 21:52 and 22:09 were all inside the check-in window. Tidewell support then used a withdrawn script, made no rehousing referral even though six comparable flats were free that night, and closed your chat by redirecting you to the host. The host recorded a no-show the next morning, after and because of its own revocation. The decision records all of this.

**What I did.** I obtained Tidewell's full booking, keypad, channel-manager, support and ledger records, plus closure and account letters from Brightwater and Calder. I lodged the arrival-guarantee review on 11 May, ahead of the 15 May deadline. After the decision I requested the host refund quoting only the decision reference, and held the Tidewell request until you texted that Calder had finished checking your account. Calder then held the transfer for a payee-name check over the weekend. I confirmed the name with Tidewell within the window and it was released. I confirmed receipt on 21 May, which closed the complaint.

**Bank details.** Your sort code and account number went only to Tidewell Payments, for the £48.50 transfer. Quaymark received none. Brightwater and Calder were given only their own account or card references.

**Two things to be aware of:**
- The £504.00 hotel cost was not claimed. Your booking falls under Guest Terms GT-2026-01, whose section 7.5 excludes self-arranged accommodation. The 125% rebooking cover was in the superseded edition and did not apply. You confirmed this by text.
- The host-recorded no-show mark was left in place at your instruction by text on 6 May, after I flagged that the review was the only chance to remove it. Under section 5.4 it stays on your profile for 12 months. The upheld decision is on record showing the host caused the access failure, but the mark itself remains.
